title: Rayleigh sphere critical points and actual unit eigenvectors
source_anchor: Boumal2023 pre-publication annotations through2026-10-08, §3.8 Example3.62 and(3.40), printed44/PDF60; §3.4 Example3.36 printed36/PDF52; induced metric/gradient conventions §§3.7–3.8
target_statement: For a real symmetric matrix A, let F(x)=xᵀAx on the unit sphere with the metric induced by the Euclidean inner product. The chosen smooth ambient quadratic extension has gradient2Ax. The tangent projector sends u to u−⟨x,u⟩x, so the sphere gradient is2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x). Its vanishing is equivalent to Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x; thus the stationary unit vectors are exactly eigenvectors of A, and every unit eigenvector is stationary.

theorem sphere_rayleigh_characterization
    (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    ∀ z : (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ,
      ((∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w =
          ⟪mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) x w, (z : E)⟫_ℝ) ↔
        (z : E) = (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)))

theorem sphere_rayleigh_stationary_iff
    (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
      A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) ∧
    (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
      ∃ μ : ℝ, Module.End.HasEigenvector A.toLinearMap μ (x : E))
